title: Exceptional Kunneth for a projection equals exceptional tensor after dualizing exchange
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and normalized constructible operation datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes with admissible structure morphism $a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and admissible projection $p_1:X\times_kY\to X$, and put $a_X:X\to s$ for the structure morphism, $p_2:X\times_kY\to Y$ for the second projection, and $\omega_Y=a_Y^!A_s$. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and assume the displayed operations lie in the finite-Tor constructible domains of [def-trf-admissibility]. Use the exceptional Kunneth map $\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y}:M\boxtimes\omega_Y\to p_1^!M$ of [def-sf-kv-maps](ii), with its specified $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ and counits. Define $\chi_{X,Y}:p_2^*\omega_Y\to p_1^!A_X$ to be the exceptional adjoint of
$$Rp_{1!}p_2^*\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}}a_X^*Ra_{Y!}\omega_Y\xrightarrow{a_X^*(\varepsilon_{a_Y})}A_X,$$
where the exchange is the compact-support exchange in the Cartesian structure square and the counit belongs to $Ra_{Y!}\dashv a_Y^!$. For any admissible $g:U\to V$ and $B,N$ in the indicated finite-Tor constructible domains, define $T_g:g^!B\otimes g^*N\to g^!(B\otimes N)$ as the $Rg_!\dashv g^!$ transpose of
$$Rg_!(g^!B\otimes g^*N)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_g^{-1}}Rg_!g^!B\otimes N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_g^!\otimes1}B\otimes N,$$
using the projection transformation and exceptional counit of [def-exchange-projection] and [def-trf-admissibility]. Then, with canonical unit identifications and signed symmetry $\sigma$,
$$\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y}=T_{p_1}\circ(\chi_{X,Y}\otimes1)\circ\sigma:
 p_1^*M\otimes p_2^*\omega_Y\longrightarrow p_1^!M.$$
Consequently the tensor--Hom transpose defining $\kappa_{M,N}$ in [def-sf-kv-maps](iv) is exactly second-factor evaluation followed by this exceptional tensor composite. For $Y=X$, the map $\chi_{X,X}$ is the $\chi$ of [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus](d), with the project's projection order.

source.place: §0.0.3, formula (0.4), and §4.4.3, diagrams (4.14)--(4.15), interchanging the two factors

proof.text: Work at the single finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$, in the specified $D^b_{ctf}$ domains. Put $Z=X\times_kY$, $p=p_1$, $H=p_2^*\omega_Y$ and $Q=p^*M\otimes H=M\boxtimes\omega_Y$. The ordered product is [def-trf-external-product], and $\alpha=\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y}$ is the map of [def-sf-kv-maps](ii). The exceptional adjunctions at $a_Y$ and $p$ are the specified constructible ones of [def-trf-admissibility], with the operation datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All the following pullbacks, tensors and compact-support images are in the domains assumed in the statement.

source.place: §0.2--§0.4, finite-Tor convention and ordered external products

proof.text: The projection transformation is the specified natural map of [def-exchange-projection]. It is invertible on the inputs used here by [prop-functor-package](5); clause (4) likewise makes the compact-support structure-square exchange invertible. For any admissible $g$, the exceptional adjunction of [def-trf-admissibility] therefore transposes $(\varepsilon_g^!\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{g;g^!B,N}^{-1}$ uniquely to $T_g:g^!B\otimes g^*N\to g^!(B\otimes N)$. In particular $T_p$ is defined at $(B,N)=(A_X,M)$ without a cohomological pre-comparison hypothesis. Write $E=a_X^*(\varepsilon_{a_Y})\operatorname{Ex}_{!,2}^{-1}:Rp_!H\to A_X$, where $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,2}:a_X^*Ra_{Y!}\omega_Y\to Rp_!H$ is this compact-support exchange. The definition of $\chi=\chi_{X,Y}$ says exactly $\varepsilon_{p,A_X}Rp_!(\chi)=E$.

Let $\sigma_{\mathrm{in}}:Q\to H\otimes p^*M$ be signed symmetry. By the definition of $T_p$ in Step 2, the $Rp_!\dashv p^!$ adjunct of $T_p(\chi\otimes1)\sigma_{\mathrm{in}}$ is
$$
(\varepsilon_{p,A_X}\otimes1_M)\operatorname{PF}_{p;p^!A_X,M}^{-1}\,Rp_!(\chi\otimes1_M)\,Rp_!(\sigma_{\mathrm{in}}).
$$
Naturality of the specified projection transformation [def-exchange-projection] in its first argument gives
$$
\operatorname{PF}_{p;p^!A_X,M}^{-1}Rp_!(\chi\otimes1_M)
=(Rp_!\chi\otimes1_M)\operatorname{PF}_{p;H,M}^{-1}.
$$
Substitute $\varepsilon_{p,A_X}Rp_!\chi=E$ from the exceptional-adjoint definition [def-trf-admissibility]. The adjunct is consequently the explicit map
$$F=(E\otimes1_M)\operatorname{PF}_{p;H,M}^{-1}Rp_!(\sigma_{\mathrm{in}}):Rp_!Q\to M.$$
Invertibility of both projection transformations is [prop-functor-package](5).

source.place: §0.3(b), (0.2), and §4.4.3, (4.15), expanding the exceptional tensor map

proof.text:
Now expand [def-sf-kv-maps](i) at $(f_1,f_2)=(\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y)$ and $(B_1,B_2)=(M,\omega_Y)$. Its notation becomes $T=U=X$, $V=W=Z$, $u=\operatorname{id}_X$, $v=p$, and its fibre-product projections are $p:Z\to X$ and $q=\operatorname{id}_Z$; $K=M$, $H=p_2^*\omega_Y$. Apply the canonical map stated in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] over the separated finite-type base $X$. Its composition comparison with $q=\operatorname{id}_Z$ is the identity by [prop-functor-package](3). Its projection transformation for $q$ and its base-change exchange for $u=\operatorname{id}_X$ are identities: in the formulas of [def-exchange-projection] the pullbacks and direct images for the identity, their units and counits, and the identity open-immersion comparisons all reduce to identities under the same normalizations. The projection notation in the relative theorem is the same concrete transformation by [def-sf-pf]. Thus, reading its remaining arrows in order, the relative map is exactly
$$
Rp_!(p^*M\otimes H)\xrightarrow{Rp_!(\sigma_{\mathrm{in}})}Rp_!(H\otimes p^*M)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{p;H,M}^{-1}}Rp_!H\otimes M
\xrightarrow{\sigma_{\mathrm{out}}}M\otimes Rp_!H.
$$
Here $\sigma_{\mathrm{out}}$ is signed symmetry. This computes the specified relative map from its defining arrows; no exterior-projection compatibility lemma is being applied.

source.place: statement, defining composite of the canonical relative product map, specialized to f=id_X and g=p_1

proof.text:
To finish the definition of $\mathrm{Ku}_!$, [def-sf-kv-maps](i) appends $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,1}^{-1}\otimes\operatorname{Ex}_{!,2}^{-1}$. The first structure square is an identity square, so $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,1}=1_M$ with the identity normalization of [prop-functor-package](3) and the formulas of [def-exchange-projection]. The second is precisely the Cartesian square with vertical arrows $p,a_Y$ and horizontal arrows $p_2,a_X$. Consequently
$$
\mathrm{Ku}_!=(1_M\otimes\operatorname{Ex}_{!,2}^{-1})\sigma_{\mathrm{out}}\operatorname{PF}_{p;H,M}^{-1}Rp_!(\sigma_{\mathrm{in}}).
$$
Use [lem-trf-exceptional-kunneth-counit] with $L_1=M$, $L_2=A_s$ and $e=1_Q$. The identity-factor exceptional counit is the identity under the normalized adjunction; the other is $\varepsilon_{a_Y}$. Thus the adjunct of $\alpha$ is
$$
(1_M\otimes a_X^*\varepsilon_{a_Y})\mathrm{Ku}_!
=(1_M\otimes E)\sigma_{\mathrm{out}}\operatorname{PF}_{p;H,M}^{-1}Rp_!(\sigma_{\mathrm{in}})=F.
$$
The last equality is naturality of signed symmetry, $(1_M\otimes E)\sigma_{\mathrm{out}}=(E\otimes1_M)$ after the tensor-unit identifications. The finite-Tor and exceptional-admissibility hypotheses of the cited counit formula hold for $\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y,p$ by the item hypotheses and the normalized identity adjunction.

source.place: §0.4, (0.4), and §4.4.3, (4.14)--(4.15), matching the specified Künneth counits

proof.text: The adjunction bijection of [def-trf-admissibility] is injective. Steps 3 and 5 compute the same adjunct $F$, so $\alpha=T_p(\chi\otimes1)\sigma_{\mathrm{in}}$. For the consequence, fix also $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ in [def-sf-kv-maps](iv). The statement of [lem-trf-kv-evaluation-formula] identifies the tensor--Hom transpose of $\kappa_{M,N}$ with $\alpha\circ e$, where $e$ reassociates $(M\boxtimes D_YN)\otimes p_2^*N$ and applies $1\otimes p_2^*\operatorname{ev}_N$ to obtain $M\boxtimes\omega_Y$. Substituting the equality just proved gives second-factor evaluation followed by $T_p(\chi\otimes1)\sigma_{\mathrm{in}}$, with precisely that lemma's signed constraints. Its coefficient, finite-Tor and admissibility assumptions are the ones fixed here.

source.place: §0.4, the second map in (0.4) and its evaluation transpose

proof.text: When $Y=X$, clause (d) of [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus] defines $\chi$ as the $Rp_{1!}\dashv p_1^!$ transpose of $a_X^*(\varepsilon_{a_X,A_s}^!)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,a_X,a_X}(\omega_X))^{-1}$. This is literally the definition of $\chi_{X,Y}$ in the statement with $Y=X$, with the same project order $p_1,p_2$. Hence $\chi_{X,X}$ is that normalized map. Only its displayed defining formula is compared; none of that node's cohomological-comparison identities or extra comparison hypotheses is invoked.

source.place: §0.4, BC in (0.4), specialized to the self-product
